tools.description: Z.ai GLM-5.3 coding/agentic model (Aug 14, 2026): same GLM-5.2 base with scaled RL post-training. 50% gain on Z.ai Code Bench, Terminal-Bench 3.0 4.6→28.3, DeepSWE v1.1 46.2→66.9. Available via GLM Coding Plan, ZCode, Claude Code, OpenCode, and the Z.ai API (model id glm-5.3).

tools.name: Entire
tools.description: Git-integrated tool that captures AI agent sessions as checkpoints alongside commits. Enables searchable history of code creation with agent context. Supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, plans for Codex.

tools.name: Oz
tools.description: Warp's cloud orchestration platform (Feb 2026) for running hundreds of parallel coding agents. Programmable, auditable, steerable with cron/webhook/API triggers. Integrates with Warp terminal.

tools.name: Muse Spark 1.1
tools.description: Meta's multimodal reasoning model for agentic tasks, launched July 9, 2026 with the new Meta Model API in public preview. Muse Spark 1.1 actively manages a 1M-token context, orchestrates parallel subagents, generalizes to MCP servers and custom skills, and combines computer use, coding, video and image understanding, structured output, and parallel tool calling.

tools.name: Grok Build
tools.description: SpaceXAI's terminal coding agent and Rust harness, open-sourced under Apache 2.0 on July 15, 2026. Grok Build understands repositories, edits files, runs commands, searches the web, and manages long-running work interactively, headlessly in CI, or through ACP-compatible editors. Its extension system supports skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, and subagents, and it can run local-first against custom inference.

tools.name: IBM Bob
tools.description: IBM's enterprise agentic software-development platform received a major July 9, 2026 update. A shared agent harness now supports native tool calling, parallel execution, specialized subagents, background tasks, and reusable governed workflows across planning, coding, testing, CI/CD, and operations. Bobalytics adds visibility into adoption, productivity, quality, usage, governance, and cost.

tools.name: Agent Script
tools.description: Salesforce's compiled language for building Agentforce agents by combining deterministic business logic with natural-language reasoning. Agent Script and the new Agentforce Builder became generally available in July 2026, while Salesforce open-sourced the Apache 2.0 toolchain: parser, linter, compiler, language server, and editor integrations. Scripts can select subagents and actions, construct context, and pin models.

tools.name: Mistral Studio Prompts & Skills
tools.description: Mistral Studio's system of record for production prompts and agent skills. Released July 9, 2026, it adds immutable versions, ownership, classification labels, comparisons, rollback, audit logs, and workspace promotion. Observability traces production outputs back to the exact asset version, while governed skills can be exposed directly as MCP servers.

tools.name: Robostral Navigate
tools.description: Mistral's first embodied-navigation model: an 8B system that follows natural-language routes using a single RGB camera with no LiDAR or depth sensor. Trained in simulation across roughly 2.4M trajectories and 350K scenes, it reached a reported 76.6% success rate on unseen R2R-CE environments and generalizes across wheeled, legged, and flying robots.

tools.name: Qwen3.8 Max
tools.weeklyHighlight: Alibaba's newest flagship MoE (2.4T / 95B active) for coding, research, and long-horizon agents
tools.description: Alibaba Qwen3.8 Max (Aug 2, 2026) — proprietary multimodal MoE flagship (~2.4T total / ~95B active, 1M context) for coding, research, and long-horizon agents via Qwen Cloud / Model Studio. Open-weight siblings followed mid-August: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8 and the dense Qwen3.8-27B (Apache-2.0) on Hugging Face.

tools.name: Agents-A1
tools.description: Shanghai AI Lab InternScience's open-weight 35B MoE agentic model (built on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B), Apache 2.0. Trained for long-horizon agent work — multi-step search, scientific research, software engineering, instruction following, and tool use — with a 256K context window and quantized GGUF variants. Claims trillion-parameter-class agent performance by scaling agent horizon rather than parameter count; SOTA on SEAL-0, FrontierScience-Research, and IFBench among open agents. Served via vLLM/SGLang; discussed widely on X and LocalLLaMA in July 2026.

tools.name: llama.cpp
tools.description: The dominant local GGUF inference stack (C/C++). Late July 2026 added native stdio MCP support in llama-server (PR #26062) so a local model can launch MCP servers, discover tools, and run agentic loops without a separate bridge — config via Claude/Cursor-style mcpServers JSON. Combined with Qwen/DeepSeek GGUFs, it becomes a full local agent harness for files, web, databases, and coding MCPs like Serena. Also popular as a cost-saving MCP worker behind Claude Code.

tools.name: Unity CLI
tools.description: Unity's terminal-native path for connecting coding agents, CI pipelines, and custom tooling to the Unity engine. Announced mid-July 2026 as free with no concurrency limits; includes MCP Mode so existing MCP-based agents work without a full rewrite while Unity MCP remains supported. Aimed at agentic game-dev and automation workflows from Claude Code, Cursor, and other CLIs.

tools.name: Claude Agent SDK
tools.description: Anthropic's official SDK for building agents on Claude (renamed from Claude Code SDK). Powers Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and third-party agents with query primitives, hooks, subagents, MCP, and A2A. Computer use (computer_toolset_20260801) and browser use plus Files/Skills APIs went GA on August 19, 2026.

tools.name: Slack Code
tools.description: Salesforce/Slack multi-player coding environment that embeds Claude Code, Devin, GitHub Copilot and Vercel agents in dedicated Slack code channels with live diffs, plans and previews.

tools.name: Muse Code
tools.description: Meta terminal coding agent powered by Muse Spark 1.2 with background sub-agents, isolated worktrees and model-agnostic harness. Available via curl installer and API.

tools.name: Muse Spark 1.2
tools.description: Meta Superintelligence Labs frontier model (Aug 5, 2026) powering Muse Code. Closed API successor to Spark 1.1 with stronger code generation and long-horizon planning; the Apache-2.0 local distill is Muse Glimmer 30B.

tools.name: DeepSeek Harness
tools.description: MIT-licensed open-source agent harness (dsh) where model adapter, tool registry and agent loop are all swappable plugins. Ships with 4 preset modes and Cordis plugin framework.

tools.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
tools.description: Google Gemini 3.7 Flash (Aug 13, 2026) — fastest Flash yet, 56 on Intelligence Index, 1st of 182 on output speed (385 tok/s), major gains on DeepSWE and coding tasks. Intro pricing $0.75/$3.75 per 1M tokens through Dec 31 2026.

tools.name: Grok 4.6
tools.description: SpaceXAI Grok 4.6 (Aug 12, 2026) post-training refresh of Grok 4.5 for long-running agents, coding, and visual/interactive work. Ties GPT-5.6 Sol at 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at $2/$6 per 1M tokens; 88.4% on Terminal-Bench v2.1 in vendor reports. Live in Cursor, Grok Build, the SpaceXAI API, OpenRouter, Vercel, and Cloudflare.

tools.name: TrueForge
tools.description: TrueFoundry MIT-licensed vendor-neutral agent harness — alternative to Claude Managed Agents with MCP, Daytona sandboxes and 20+ model providers at claimed half operating cost.

tools.name: Grok Bot
tools.description: Cursor/SpaceXAI early-beta AI teammates that each get a persistent cloud computer with a browser, filesystem, and terminal. Bots sign in to real tools, coordinate in parallel, and only return for approval. Available on desktop and iOS for SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Teams Premium.

tools.name: Muse Glimmer 30B
tools.description: Meta Superintelligence Labs 30B Apache-2.0 multimodal agentic model distilled from Muse Spark for local deployment. Runs on a single 24 GB GPU (~4-bit); 76.0% SWE-bench Verified, 51.2% SWE-bench Pro, 75.5 MCP Atlas. Ships BF16 weights, k-quants, a DFlash speculative-decoding drafter (233 tok/s on RTX 5090), and a perception encoder.

tools.name: Chroma Foundation
tools.description: Chroma's research-preview agent memory product (Aug 20, 2026). Builds a self-improving wiki from Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Slack sessions on top of ChromaDB and the Context-1 retrieval model. SOC 2 Type 2; starts at $30/user/month on Chroma Cloud.

tools.name: Junie Local
tools.description: JetBrains on-device inference for Junie (Aug 24, 2026). One /local command downloads a Qwen3.6-27B 4-bit MLX runtime (~20 GB) and runs the full coding agent on Apple M5 Macs with 64 GB RAM — no credits, no cloud, code stays on the machine.

tools.name: OpenClaw
tools.description: Open-source self-hosted personal AI assistant (MIT) that runs a local Gateway and meets you in WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, iMessage, Signal, and other chats. ~387K GitHub stars; skills via ClawHub; model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, local). Formerly Clawdbot/Moltbot.

tools.name: Kitesurf
tools.description: Cloudflare's agent-first browser that runs in V8 isolates on Workers. Speaks CDP so Puppeteer, Playwright, and MCP clients work unchanged. 3–7× less CPU/memory than Chromium on screenshots and HTML extraction; free during beta via Browser Run.

tools.name: Cloudflare OS
tools.description: Apache-2.0 agent workspace Cloudflare open-sourced from its internal operating model. Combines an agent chat UI preloaded with company context, sandboxed 'gadgets' (small apps), and Gatekeepers that scope MCP-style tool access with human approval for destructive actions.

tools.name: WebMCP
tools.description: Cloudflare developer-preview protocol that gives any website an agent-callable interface without new origin APIs. Complements MCP by making pages discoverable and usable by browser agents while the human stays in control.

tools.name: GitLab Duo Agent Platform
tools.description: GitLab's agentic DevSecOps platform. GitLab 19.3 (Aug 20, 2026) made the Dedicated AI Gateway GA so Duo agents run in-region with BYO models, plus Flow Creator Agent (plain-language custom flows) and agentic SAST vulnerability resolution.

tools.name: Claude Cowork
tools.description: Anthropic's Claude Code-style agent for knowledge work. Runs multi-step tasks across files, calendar, email, Slack, and the browser on desktop, web, and mobile. Computer use and browser toolsets went GA on the Claude API on August 19, 2026.

tools.name: Embabel
tools.description: JVM agent framework by Spring creator Rod Johnson. Models agents as typed goals, actions, and conditions with a planner (GOAP) on top of Spring AI. 1.0 GA July 2026; 1.5.0 (Aug 12) adds Spring Boot 4 / Spring AI 2 support. Apache-2.0, Kotlin + Java.

tools.name: Qwen3.8-27B
tools.description: Alibaba's Apache-2.0 dense 27B vision-language model in the Qwen3.8 generation. Native 262K context (extensible to 1M), hybrid Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention, thinking control. Vendor-reported 73.0 Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 61.7 SWE-bench Pro — a compact open coder that runs on a 4090-class GPU.

tools.name: NeMo Switchyard
tools.description: NVIDIA open-source routing library that sends each step of an agent workflow to the most capable and efficient model available. Ships with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning; partners include LangChain, Cognition, Kong, Boomi, and Siemens.

tools.name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813
tools.description: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 (Aug 13, 2026) — official ~1.6T MoE (49B active) MIT open-weight flagship with a 1M-token context, Responses API, and reasoning-effort controls. Complements the cheaper V4-Flash-0731 line for heavier agentic and coding workloads.
